providers.sourceStatusReason: Unofficial WATCH source: every scheduled, startup, restart, ordinary manual, and dedicated-repair Claude collection first rereads exact native credentials noninteractively, preferring a usable file session. If recovery is required, that collection has one bounded opportunity for screen-unlocked native authorization and, for expired or rejected credentials, one Claude Code owner /usage launch. Denial aborts the current attempt without a loop; the next default five-minute cycle may retry. Only claudeAiOauth is eligible, MCP is forbidden, and only a successful live response is fresh.
documentation: https://registry.npmjs.org/@anthropic-ai/claude-code-darwin-arm64/2.1.280 (reset query and cedar_ember grant schema; published SHA-512 integrity verified)
providers.credentialPersistence: Claude-owned ~/.claude/.credentials.json, <config dir>/.credentials.json, and native Keychain generic-password services Claude Code-credentials and Claude Code-credentials-<sha256(config dir)[0:8]> with account NSUserName(); Token Jar performs exact read-only access. Profile results (keyed by access-token digest) and reset-ticket results (30 minutes) are kept in process memory only, never on disk or in the Keychain. Claude Code alone may rotate its stores under .oauth_refresh.lock during a bounded collection recovery
tokenTankIO: Discover sign-ins: the default login, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, and every ~/.claude-* directory that lies inside the home directory and holds .claude.json or .credentials.json. Each directory uses Keychain service Claude Code-credentials-<first 8 hex of SHA-256(directory path)> with account NSUserName(), else <dir>/.credentials.json. Identity (accountUuid, emailAddress) comes from that directory's .claude.json oauthAccount (16 MiB cap), else the profile response; sign-ins with the same accountUuid or the same access token are collected once

Read claudeAiOauth only from ~/.claude/.credentials.json and the native generic-password service Claude Code-credentials with account NSUserName(); never match another same-service account. Require user:profile, finite positive expiry more than 60 seconds away, and reject MCP

Every Claude collection first rereads the exact file noninteractively, then the exact Keychain account when no usable file session exists. Retain rejected-token identity independently per file/Keychain slot and adopt a changed valid external token. On expiry at 60 seconds or less or usage HTTP 401, retry usage at most once only with a changed token; HTTP 403 never recovers

Scheduled refresh, ordinary user refresh, startup, restart, and dedicated repair all use collection context allowsClaudeRecovery=true. isUserInitiated truthfully records the trigger and does not control recovery authority; the default schedule remains five minutes

When a bounded recovery cannot supply a usable session, retain the prior in-memory snapshot only as stale and expose typed repairClaudeConnection for unavailable Keychain access or a session still needing recovery. Missing or revoked login requires source-owner sign-in

Each collection has at most one recovery opportunity. After the screen-unlocked guard, it may attempt native authorization once and, for expired or rejected credentials, launch one bounded owner process. Denial, cancellation, lock, or authorization failure aborts the current attempt without another CLI or prompt loop; the next scheduled collection may try again

The localized Repair Claude Connection / Claude 연결 복구 action starts an immediate manual collection under the same limits. Concurrent repair callers coalesce. The UI immediately shows pending manual repair or active collection progress with native approval guidance, without inferring internal phases

Claude Code may show its own permission UI during the single bounded owner launch. The owner uses fixed absolute executable candidates, an empty mode-0700 workspace, minimal fixed environment, fixed safe-mode/no-tools arguments, fixed bounded timeout, and the official owner refresh lock

Prompt veto precedes readiness and success. Require readiness plus shift+tab before exactly /usage and a completed panel plus one second quiet; trust is accepted only in the verified-empty workspace and never after /usage. Completed flow sends Esc then /exit with five-second grace; the post-usage hard deadline is passive and pre-readiness cleanup supplies no input

GET only https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage, optionally same-token /api/oauth/profile, and optionally same-token /api/oauth/usage?cedar_ember=1&skip_spend=1 with a 15-second maximum. Require the exact official usage transport User-Agent claude-cli/2.1.280 (external, cli); the separate claude-code/2.1.280 identity was observed to return ineligible_reason:surface and no grants. The reset request uses only the exact fixed query, no body, no authentication recovery, and no redemption POST. Parse cedar_ember.grants id/resets_left/starts_at/ends_at; preserve explicit counts without local-date ownership filtering. Empty grants without eligible:true, absent or malformed metadata stay unknown without discarding valid usage. Do not import browser cookies, automate login/browser approval, scrape PTY usage, call Admin or inference APIs, use ~/.claude.json cached usage, or directly POST/write/copy/cache a Claude token

Recovery budgets apply per account per collection: at most one native authorization and one owner /usage launch for each sign-in. A config-directory account's owner launch receives CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<dir> so Claude Code repairs that sign-in, not the default

Supplemental requests are cached in memory only: /api/oauth/profile once per access token; the reset-ticket query at most every 30 minutes per account (a failed query keeps the previous value; an account-identity change invalidates it). Tickets whose ends_at has passed are removed from display and the summary count is recomputed from the remaining tickets

providers.selectedSource: Read-only Grok-owned ~/.grok/auth.json sessions (every official OIDC scope or legacy sign-in entry, deduplicated by user_id); primary cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1/billing?format=credits per account; when a session is expired (within 60 seconds) or the first proxy request returns 401/403, run the installed Grok CLI once per collection (`grok models`) so the CLI renews under its own lock, then reread the file and retry the proxy once; only when a successful proxy response leaves usage unknown, bearer-only POST https://grok.com/grok_api_v2.GrokBuildBilling/GetGrokCreditsConfig with the same session bearer and a 6-second timeout
providers.sourceStatusReason: Decision 2026-09-29, rule (b): Token Jar no longer sends refresh grants or writes auth.json. Evidence (Grok CLI 1.0.44 official stable build, sha256 b637a934…7c28, exercised with fake credentials and a local mock issuer): the CLI re-reads auth.json under a blocking flock on ~/.grok/auth.json.lock before refreshing and adopts a sibling's rotated token, but Token Jar's former separate .token-tank-auth.lock did not exclude the CLI, and a CLI invalid_grant without an observable sibling rotation deletes the auth entry, so the race was not proven safe. `grok models` renews an expired token non-interactively without model usage (verified with fake credentials); its exit status is 0 even when renewal fails, so Token Jar rereads the file and requires a usable token.
providers.rejectedAlternative: Direct refresh_token grants to auth.x.ai and any auth.json write (removed; the audit fails on oauth2/token, grant_type, or the legacy lock name), browser-cookie imports, Grok ACP stdio, interactive CLI automation, prompts, manual-token UI, local-session estimates, xAI Management API/prepaid-balance calls, Keychain token caches, backups, and other secret stores. The older Grok Build ACP x.ai/billing probe returned JSON-RPC -32601 on official Grok 1.0.13.
documentation: https://x.ai/cli/install.sh and https://x.ai/cli/stable (1.0.44 binary inspected and exercised with fake credentials, 2026-09-29)
providers.credentialPersistence: Grok-owned ~/.grok/auth.json and ~/.grok/auth.json.lock; Token Jar only reads auth.json and never writes, copies, or rotates it. A .token-tank-auth.lock left by an older Token Jar is left untouched
tokenTankIO: Open only ~/.grok/auth.json read-only (O_NOFOLLOW, owner-only permissions, single link, 64 KiB cap). Every https://auth.x.ai::<client> entry with issuer https://auth.x.ai and matching oidc_client_id, plus the legacy https://accounts.x.ai/sign-in entry, is an account; entries sharing a user_id are collected once; xai::api_key is ignored

When an account's access token expires within 60 seconds, or after one credits proxy 401/403, run the first executable among ~/.grok/bin/grok, ~/.local/bin/grok, /opt/homebrew/bin/grok, /usr/local/bin/grok with the single argument `models`, from an empty mode-0700 temporary directory, stdin closed, a fixed minimal environment without GROK_* overrides, a 30-second limit, and a 256 KiB output cap; at most once per collection

Reread auth.json after the CLI exits; a still-expired or still-rejected account reports RecoveryAction.runSourceCLI ("Run the Grok CLI once to renew") and is reread on the transient-failure schedule (60 seconds, backing off to 5 minutes)
HTTPS GET https://cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1/billing?format=credits with each account's ephemeral bearer; after a 401/403 and the reread, retry that account's proxy exactly once

Only when a successful proxy response leaves usage unknown, POST https://grok.com/grok_api_v2.GrokBuildBilling/GetGrokCreditsConfig with the same bearer, a 5-byte empty gRPC-web data frame (00 00 00 00 00), no cookies, and a 6-second timeout

Preserve proxy reset, source metadata, and account identity; adopt a published web percentage, or an omitted proto3 scalar as zero only for a structurally complete response with a recognized current weekly/monthly period containing the refresh time; otherwise retain unknown, including a failed fallback
Expose published creditUsagePercent or the same-row on-demand used/cap ratio under the credits quota
Display each account's optional email in memory; one failed account never replaces another account's data
providers.liveValidation: 2026-09-29: the read-only and CLI-renewal decision rests on fake-credential experiments against the official 1.0.44 binary (sibling-rotation adoption under flock, invalid_grant entry deletion, `grok models` renewal and exit status); package tests cover read-only behavior, one CLI run per collection, multi-account discovery, and the CLI invocation contract. No real Grok account was exercised: the Grok CLI and a Grok login are absent on the development host.
providers.mutationRisk: Token Jar performs no credential mutation. The Grok CLI it launches may rotate its own auth.json under its own lock, and on invalid_grant the CLI itself may delete the entry, exactly as when the user runs the CLI.
providers.releaseBlocker: WATCH: live-validate a naturally expired session renewed by `grok models`, a real proxy 401/403, multiple signed-in scopes, and the packaged final candidate; complete CI, signing, and notarization evidence

refreshPolicy.scheduler: Per-provider next check time evaluated on a 15-second wall-clock tick; a pool starts due providers as slots free up (concurrency limit 2).
refreshPolicy.success: Next check 5 minutes after a successful collection.
refreshPolicy.transientFailure: Transient failures (network, offline, source unavailable, schema, expired session waiting for the owner CLI) retry after 60 seconds, doubling per consecutive failure up to 5 minutes.
refreshPolicy.rateLimited: HTTP 429 waits for the larger of Retry-After and 60 seconds; Retry-After also bounds manual refresh.
refreshPolicy.authenticationActionRequired: Quiet credential reread every 60 seconds; Claude recovery budgets are unchanged.
refreshPolicy.partialAccountFailure: A snapshot with failed accounts retries per the failing accounts' rules; accounts needing sign-in alone keep the 5-minute cadence.
refreshPolicy.manualRefreshFloor: A manual refresh within 30 seconds of the provider's last collection start reuses the current state; Repair Claude Connection is exempt.
refreshPolicy.surfaceOpen: Opening the usage window or menu-bar panel collects providers whose last success is older than 60 seconds, subject to the manual floor and Retry-After.
refreshPolicy.sleepAndNetwork: No scheduled collection while the Mac sleeps. After wake, collection waits up to 30 seconds for a satisfied NWPathMonitor path. When the path returns, providers stale from network-class failures become due at once.
refreshPolicy.evidence: Package tests SchedulerTests (ManualClock and injected SystemActivityMonitoring events).
